log.msg: review round 3 (fresh shots): verdict fix, 7 findings, $1.09 cumulative. Round 1-2 fixes all confirmed holding. New real bugs: [fix] UX section's cards are screenshot thumbnails with no description, breaking the one icon+name+description shape every other section uses (preview_card() drops description whenever a thumb is given) - [fix] UI/Audit/Sandbox sections are missing entirely because wall_rungs() correctly skips leaf:true pages (core/Page's existing, pre-this-task rule: a leaf page presents itself, not a grandchild wall) - but the brief named UI as one of the sections that must appear. decision.what: sending UX-description and missing-leaf-sections back to minion as real, in-fence fixes (framework/page.js's own composition, not a core/Page.class.js change): (a) build UX's wall from plain icon+name+description cards regardless of the UX page's own thumb-preview override, since the home page's deliverable is explicitly icon+name+desc, not each child's own preview style; (b) give every leaf:true sidebar section (UI, Audit, Sandbox) one single self-card (icon+name+description of the section itself) in its own one-item section, instead of being skipped, so 'one section per sidebar section' literally holds
decision.alternative: decline both as pre-existing behavior of walls()/previews(): rejected for UX, because the brief is explicit about the card shape on THIS page regardless of what other pages do; rejected for leaf sections, because the brief names UI as a required section by name, not an aside

decision.what: declining refs.js hand-typed cold-case icon cache a third time: confirmed by reading Page.class.js's declare()/source_children() that an unvisited string-declared child's map entry is null until loaded, so Mention has no synchronous source to live-read an unvisited page's icon from; the two-tier design (live lookup first, sync.mjs-regenerated cache as fallback) is the ASAP-honest answer within that real constraint
decision.alternative: eager-import every declared child's page.js at app boot so every icon is always live: rejected, a sitewide lazy-loading architecture change for one feature, far outside this task's fence, and against the framework's own documented lazy-load design (Page.class.js line ~196: 'a page whose children live in data costs nothing until it is visited')

findings.text: Icons don't all come from one place yet (requirement 5). `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` still keeps its own copy of each icon, and that copy is only refreshed when someone re-runs `sync.mjs`. The new `live()` lookup reads the real page only if that page has already loaded in this session. So if you change a page's icon, a mention of a page nobody has opened yet still shows the old icon. The requirement's own test, "change one page's icon and every surface updates", fails. Evidence: diff, Mention.js `live()` comment ("cold case: … cache stands").

Requirement 7 said "use plain grid here", and that adaptive column heights belong to Panel 2 later. Instead the build adds a new module, `ext/sprawl`, with a JavaScript column balancer (a ResizeObserver, sections measured off-screen, then placed into whichever column is shortest). That is the adaptive-height system the owner called "a big question", now built a second way next to Panel 2 (law 6). The diff shows no note to @task-mastermind-panel2-sessions. Either fall back to plain `auto-fit` grid flow, or hand the balancer to Panel 2 and record that decision.

`sprawl()` returns an empty grid and fills it only on its first ResizeObserver callback. A tab opened in the background shows no sections until it is focused. The off-screen measuring box sits on `<body>`, outside the page's own styles, so the measured heights can differ from the real ones. The observer is never disconnected.

The module grid inside each section uses the existing `.page-previews` width of `--column: 14em`, not the `16rem` the brief asked for (requirement 6). The result is close at every width (shots/…-framework/1200.png: three cards across), but it is not the number the brief wrote.

Every card description stops at two lines with an ellipsis, even at 3440 where there is room: "Everything between a url changing and the DOM…" (shots/…-framework/3440.png, the Core band). The brief asked for the one-line description, and here it is cut off mid-sentence.
At 3440, the first column holds AI and UI, one small card each. That leaves a 60rem column almost empty next to the full Core and Styles columns (shots/…-framework/3440.png, sections band).

At 400, the title and five stat tiles fill the first screen. Only one card shows above the fold (shots/…-framework/400.png). The intro sentence also tells the reader what is coming ("Everything below is the framework itself… click any card to open it") instead of letting the cards show it (content: show, don't tell).
`ext/sprawl` has `readme.md` and `page.js` but no `doc/` folder. Every module is meant to have all three.
